newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: GOLF-TIRED MONTGOMERIE STRUGGLING TO KEEP PACE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TIRED MONTGOMERIE STRUGGLING TO KEEP PACE.

text.p: Colin Montgomerie is feeling the strain as he tries to become Europe's top golfer for the fourth successive year and hold off the challenge of main rival Ian Woosnam.

The Scot just survived the halfway cut in the European Open with a birdie at the 18th hole at the K Club near Dublin, but must keep going if he wants to pip Woosnam, currently 141,000 pounds ($220,000) behind with three tournaments to go.
"I've almost had enough," said Montgomerie, whose 74 in occasionally torrential rain left him 10 shots behind co-leaders Costantino Rocca of Italy and England's Jim Payne.

"It's putting a lot of pressure on me, my wife and my children. I am never at home and I won't be chasing it hard anymore. If it happens again it happens, but I am going to make my schedule next year and stick with it."
The good news for Montgomerie was that Woosnam also struggled before grabbing a birdie at the last for a 72 and a two-over aggregate score of 146, one shot ahead of his rival.

In the separate race for the #125,000 top prize on Sunday, Payne and Rocca lead by a shot from England's Paul Broadhurst, Spain's Miguel Angel Martin and Ireland's Padraig Harrington, who followed his opening 65 with a 73 today.
Payne was out for several months following a spinal fusion operation in September 1994 but, having won the Italian Open in May, is now a serious contender after shooting 68 and 69.
Rocca was bitterly disappointed to finish only with a 70, dropping two late shots and missing a host of other birdie chances.
One player not returning for the weekend, yet able to drown his sorrows was New Zealander Michael Campbell.

He is currently heading for a return to the qualifying school a year after finishing third in the Open at St Andrews, but despite missing the cut left with four cases of Irish whiskey, a reward for two eagles at the 18th.
